free_tier.stated: No free trial, stated in the provider's own words on two pages, while a third page offers three days of free access and the refund documentation invites a request to discuss free testing, so the provider publishes two answers at once. What is real is hourly billing on every virtual server: the machine is charged from delivery to cancellation, so a few hours of a full machine cost a few roubles and the unused remainder of a month returns to the balance as credit rather than as money. The cheapest shape is vm.v2-pico at 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, 40 GB SSD, a 1 Gbit/s port and 3 TB of traffic included, for RUB 490 a month.

chaining: Hourly billing is the composition this provider offers: at RUB 490 a month a machine costs about RUB 0.67 an hour, so the whole catalogue can be benchmarked for the price of a coffee, and 3 TB of included traffic on a 1 Gbit/s port is the cheapest per-terabyte allowance found among evaluated providers at RUB 163 a terabyte.

limits.value: The included traffic is the first thing to fail at the high volume: 3 TB a month is about 100 GB a day, and the port at 1 Gbit/s could move thirty times that, so the allowance rather than the link is the ceiling.
